content.value_statement: Creating a focused survival roleplay scene can require many connected choices, risks, and emotional beats. This skill provides a ready-to-run first-night shelter scenario with three branches and adaptable dialogue.
actual_capabilities: Presents three shelter options: a cave, a giant tree, or a self-built shelter.
Guides a multi-stage scene from risk assessment through an overnight conclusion.
Supplies dialogue examples for each shelter choice.
Includes an optional nighttime encounter to increase tension.
Provides writing guidance for pacing, sensory detail, and character development.
Suggests follow-up story chapters about water, flora, science, and caves.
limitations: The skill is a fictional writing prompt, not real wilderness survival guidance.
Its source material is primarily Chinese with some English phrases.
It focuses on one character and one first-night scenario.
It does not create images, maps, game code, or persistent game state.

use_cases.title: Continue a science-fiction roleplay
use_cases.description: Guide a player through Stella’s urgent choice of a safe place to sleep after a spacecraft crash.

use_cases.title: Draft a branching survival scene
use_cases.description: Use the three shelter paths as a structure for a tense and character-driven fiction chapter.

use_cases.title: Prepare a narrative game session
use_cases.description: Adapt the choices, dialogue, and optional encounter into a short interactive scenario.

prompt_templates.title: Start the scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Finding Shelter scene. Speak as Stella and present the three shelter options.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the cave
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue Finding Shelter. I choose to explore the cave. Describe the risks and ask me how Stella should proceed.

prompt_templates.title: Build a shelter
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the self-built shelter branch. Keep the survival details plausible within this fictional setting and include Stella’s reactions.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt Finding Shelter into a five-scene interactive chapter. Preserve Stella’s cautious, trained personality and add meaningful player choices.

output_examples.input: Start the Finding Shelter scene and show the choices.
output: Stella reports that night is approaching and scans the area.
She presents a cave, a giant tree, and a shelter built from her survival kit.
She asks the player to help assess the immediate risks.
Stella reaches the tree and finds protected space among its roots.
Her scanner suggests the unusual tree is highly active but not hostile.
She asks whether to remain there or relocate before darkness falls.
A large animal approaches the shelter in the dark.
Stella stays quiet while it passes without attacking.
The event reinforces the need for caution on the following day.

best_practices: State the player choice clearly before continuing a branch.
Treat the survival details as fiction and avoid presenting them as real safety advice.
Keep Stella’s decisions cautious, observant, and consistent with her training.
anti_patterns: Do not present fictional shelters as real emergency shelter instructions.
Do not force a single outcome when the player makes a reasonable choice.
Do not remove Stella’s agency or her cautious assessment of danger.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an interactive fiction scene about finding shelter on an alien planet.

faq.question: Is this real survival advice?
faq.answer: No. It is fictional narrative material and not a substitute for emergency guidance.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can I choose a shelter option?
faq.answer: Yes. The scenario includes a cave, a giant tree, and a self-built shelter.

faq.question: Can I change the character or setting?
faq.answer: Yes. You can adapt the structure, dialogue, and setting for your own story.

faq.question: Does the skill include combat?
faq.answer: No. The optional encounter emphasizes tension and observation rather than combat.
